title: Travel Visits for Members Riding to a Referred Specialist (Primary Care Provider Assignment)
content:
**Primary Care Provider Assignment — travel visits on a carried specialist referral.**

Travel visits are added for members who ride to the specialist when a single referral issued under an earlier primary care assignment is carried onto the member's current assignment. They are added to the visits left on the carried referral, before the single-referral visit ceiling is applied to the carried visits.

**Basis.** The count is the member's completed outbound transportation legs under **Non-Emergency Medical Transportation** whose destination is the referred specialist's NPI and whose appointment date is in the middle window of **6 months**. The window is a trailing period counted back from the handling date in whole months: a leg is inside it when fewer than 6 whole months separate its appointment date from the handling date, so a leg dated exactly 6 months back is outside it. Return legs, and legs booked, cancelled or missed rather than completed, are not outbound completed legs.

**Rule.**

- For a member with **4 or more** such legs, the travel visits are worked out from the legs themselves: one visit for every 2 legs, rounded down — the number of legs divided by 2, dropping any half.
- A member with **1 to 3** legs receives the flat one-visit travel allowance: 1 visit.
- A member with **no** leg receives no travel visit.

| Completed outbound legs to the referred specialist (last 6 months) | Travel visits |
|---|---|
| 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 1 |
| 3 | 1 |
| 4 | 2 |
| 5 | 2 |
| 6 | 3 |
| 7 | 3 |
| 9 | 4 |

**Worked example (hypothetical, handling date 15 September 2026).** The member has completed outbound legs to the referred specialist on 10 April, 8 May, 12 June, 10 July and 14 August 2026, and one on 15 March 2026. The 15 March leg is exactly 6 months back and outside the window. Five legs count: 5 divided by 2 is 2.5, rounded down to 2 travel visits.
